englishDefinition: A writer or creator who presents another person's words, ideas, or work as their own without proper attribution.

usage.english: The journal retracted the article after discovering the author was a plagiarist.

englishDefinition: Worn-out, commonplace remarks or clichés that lack originality or depth.

usage.english: The committee dismissed the proposal because the minister's response was full of platitudes and no concrete measures.

englishDefinition: A system of government in which power is effectively held by the wealthy.

usage.english: Critics warned that unchecked lobbying would steer the country toward a plutocracy rather than a representative democracy.

englishDefinition: The custom or practice of a woman being married to more than one husband at the same time.

usage.english: Anthropologists documented instances of polyandry among certain Himalayan communities.

englishDefinition: The practice of having more than one spouse (husband or wife) simultaneously.

usage.english: Debates on family law often address the legal and social implications of polygamy.

urduMeanings: مصنف کی وفات کے بعد شائع ہونے والا
englishDefinition: Published, released, or occurring after the death of the originator (e.g., a writer's work appearing after their death).

usage.english: The committee included several posthumous essays when compiling the author's collected works.

englishDefinition: A medical examination of a body conducted after death to determine cause of death (autopsy).

usage.english: The forensic team performed a postmortem to establish the cause of death for the inquiry.

englishDefinition: Something or someone that comes before and signals or paves the way for a later event or development; a forerunner.

usage.english: The invention of the telegraph was a precursor to modern long-distance communication systems.

englishDefinition: The principal character or leading figure in a drama, novel, or story; the main actor in an event or movement.

usage.english: In the exam essay, identify how the protagonist's choices drive the novel's central conflict.

englishDefinition: A tendency to be quarrelsome, combative, or eager to fight.

usage.english: The politician's pugnacity during debates alienated moderate voters.

englishDefinition: A victory won at such a great cost that it is tantamount to defeat; success achieved with devastating losses.

usage.english: Historians describe the campaign as a pyrrhic victory because the army suffered irreparable losses despite winning the battle.

englishDefinition: To restore to life or to reactivate something that has become inactive.

usage.english: The government reanimated the stalled infrastructure project by providing new funding.

englishDefinition: Excessive adherence to official rules and formalities that delays action.

usage.english: Red-tapism delayed the approval of the emergency relief funds.

englishDefinition: Payment or compensation given for work or services.

usage.english: Remuneration for public servants is set according to the national pay scale.

englishDefinition: Reserved in speech; reluctant to speak or disclose information.

usage.english: The minister remained reticent about the details of the policy change.

englishDefinition: Relating to or looking back on past events.

usage.english: The parliamentary committee ordered a retrospective review of last decade's legislation.

englishDefinition: An act that violates or shows disrespect toward sacred persons, places, or things.

usage.english: Vandalism of the shrine was condemned as a serious sacrilege.

englishDefinition: A person who walks while asleep (a sleepwalker).

usage.english: The somnambulist was found wandering the garden at dawn and taken home safely.

englishDefinition: A person who talks while asleep (a sleep‑talker).

usage.english: During the sleep study the somniloquist repeatedly uttered phrases he could not recall in the morning.

englishDefinition: To make free of germs or microorganisms.

usage.english: Hospitals sterilize surgical instruments before every operation to prevent infection.

englishDefinition: Stoic: a person indifferent to pleasure or pain; Stoicism: the practice or philosophy of self‑denial and endurance.

usage.english: Stoicism teaches self-control in adversity; a stoic faces hardship without complaint.

englishDefinition: To cause two or more events to occur at the same time.

usage.english: The technicians synchronized the cameras so all footage would start simultaneously.

englishDefinition: Not able to be tamed or domesticated.

usage.english: The untamable wild horse resisted every attempt at training.

englishDefinition: To waver between options or opinions; to be indecisive.

usage.english: When faced with two policy options, the minister vacillated and delayed a decision.

englishDefinition: Open to bribery; corrupt.

usage.english: The inquiry exposed several venal officials who took bribes.

englishDefinition: A minor fault or offense that can be forgiven.

usage.english: A venial mistake on the report did not affect the final grade.

englishDefinition: Using exactly the same words; word for word.

usage.english: The witness repeated the suspect's statement verbatim to the police.

englishDefinition: Using more words than necessary; wordy in style.

usage.english: The candidate's verbose answer lost marks because the examiner expected a concise response.

englishDefinition: A person with long experience in military service or any occupation.

usage.english: The veteran civil servant was consulted for reforms because of his decades of administrative experience.

englishDefinition: To show that something or someone is right, justified, or free from blame.

usage.english: Fresh documentation may vindicate the policy decision questioned during the parliamentary debate.

englishDefinition: Open to attack, harm, or risk; susceptible to injury or adverse effects.

usage.english: Poor infrastructure makes rural populations particularly vulnerable to natural disasters.
